Notes

统称

统称 means grouping several things under one name. The refrain does more than name a subject: it labels what follows—rules, beatings, scolding and forced-looking behavior. 'We call it all discipline' preserves that act of naming, and the later verse supplies the explicit 'we.'

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 統稱
  • Chinese lyric transcript
魔术师

Miracles are scarce, and then the magician goes home: the wording moves from something supernatural to somebody who performs illusions. What remains receives the name “discipline.” Read together, the lines let that tidy label replace any promise of transformation or rescue.

  • Lyric text
一堆散沙

Loose sand is an established idiom for people who cannot hold together as a group. Each grain remains separate. Placing it after 体系, 'system,' sets up the verse's tension: organization promises cohesion, while the next lines show the punishment used to enforce it.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 一片散沙
  • Chinese lyric transcript
梦到后

The final 后 means 'after' and can carry the dream clause into the next question: 'After you dream about it in your sleep, wouldn't you be afraid?' The object of the dream is left unstated. This reading keeps the thought connected without inventing a particular nightmare.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 後
  • Chinese lyric transcript
油还加不加

加油 means adding fuel and is also the everyday cheer 'keep going!' or 'come on!' Here the question separates 油, 'fuel,' from 加, 'add.' The coming car scene makes refueling literal, while the encouragement meaning creates an uneasy echo beside the trembling legs.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 加油
  • Chinese lyric transcript
说走就走的旅行

说走就走的旅行 became a familiar phrase for the freedom to drop everything and travel; a 2015 China Tourism Academy speech discussed it as a youth buzzword. Here the passengers sit behind a driver who cannot see. The cheerful slogan lands inside a scene where they have little control over where they are going.

  • China Tourism Academy: Dai Bin on the phrase at COTTM2015
  • Chinese lyric transcript
